precepts.text: The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead. So our people, when we got conquered and overthrown and colonised by our oppressors over the course of time up until now, we wandered out of understanding and now we are the congregation of the dead. We are a spiritually dead people, alive and well, but inside we are dead, destroyed, divisive, self-defeating, self-hating, self-detrimental.
precepts.point: Then said he unto me, Prophesy unto the wind, prophesy, son of man, and say to the wind, Thus saith the Lord God; Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live. So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army. That is the unity Malcolm was talking about. That unity of us standing together, standing as one, in one mind, one understanding, one God, one race, one nation of people. Not divided or split apart. That is the army God is raising up slowly amongst us. An empire within an empire. That is what we are becoming slowly. And do not think eyes are not on us. Eyes are on us outside of here, and eyes are on us in here too.

note.label: Foundational Babylonian Advocates: Division Among the Dispersion

precepts.why:
The bones in the valley were “very dry”: no nourishment, no understanding, no water. Solomon shows how a people come to be counted among the dead: “The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.”

That is our people. When we got conquered and overthrown and colonised by our oppressors, over the course of time up until now, we wandered out of understanding, and now we are the congregation of the dead. It is the same as waxing old and being defiled with the dead in a strange land.

We are a spiritually dead people. Alive and well on the outside, but inside we are dead: destroyed, divisive, self-defeating, self-hating, self-detrimental. That is why the bones are dry.

So when the Lord asks, “Son of man, can these bones live?”, the answer is the understanding we wandered away from. Ezekiel is told, “O ye dry bones, hear the word of the Lord.” What must be brought to these bones is the word of God, not the word of some hustler, some ex-pimp, some pastor, preacher or rapper. The words of the Bible. The breath is the word of God, and only that understanding can bring the congregation of the dead back to life.

precepts.text: The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead. The white man, the Arabs, the Chinese, they made sure we would lose our way, lose our identity, lose our self-worth. We would forget the laws of God. So therefore we are in the congregation of the dead.
precepts.point: Where also our Lord was crucified. Brothers always skip over that part. Christ was crucified in Jerusalem. So what is it saying? That this is a spiritual Jerusalem, a figurative Jerusalem. It is not literal, but this is where our Lord was crucified. How so? We do not want that black Christ that taught the commandments to gather the twelve. We do not want that guy. Kill that. We want this European guy that came from France who loves everybody, that died for black people. That is what we want. That is also where our Lord was crucified.

note.label: Prison House of Shadows

precepts.why:
“And their dead bodies”. What makes them dead bodies, when we are not literally dead? This ties in with Deuteronomy 28:48, where the yoke of iron would not be taken off our necks until we were destroyed: destroyed means dead. We are dead. Proverbs shows how: “The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.”

The white man, the Arabs, the Chinese made sure we would lose our way, lose our identity, lose our self-worth, and forget the laws of God. So we are in the congregation of the dead.

That is what the intergenerational trauma shows: economic and housing insecurity, being stereotyped and held to unequal standards, sleep problems, elevated stress and high blood pressure, and brothers always troubled without knowing why. Many think Deuteronomy 28 doesn't affect us, but it passes down across whole generations.

Those are the dead bodies lying in the street of the great city: the Israelites who wandered from the understanding of God's laws, now in graves of religion (Baptist, Pentecostal, Seventh Day Adventist, Jehovah's Witness) and graves of politics (Republican and Democrat). As we wake up to the truth that we are the Israelites, we are coming out of those graves partially, not 100%, because fear, mistrust, chronic stress and low self-esteem are still among us.

precepts.text: The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead. We wandered out of the way of understanding God's laws; we are the congregation of the dead.
precepts.point: And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city. What is the biblical name of the great city?

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
Whose “dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city”? We are not physically dead, but mentally and spiritually we are a dead race of people. Proverbs shows how we got that way: “The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.”

We wandered out of the way of understanding God's laws. So we are the congregation of the dead, and our dead bodies lie in the streets of Babylon the great, America, the spiritual Sodom and Egypt.

The dead bodies of Revelation 11:8 are not a graveyard somewhere; they are our people, living in the street of the great city but dead to the laws of God.

precepts.text: The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead. When you keep doing the same thing over and over and wonder why life is not working out for you, this is what spiritual men and women are supposed to examine: could it be that you have a secret life?
precepts.point: To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to the Lord than sacrifice. They thought sacrifice was going to absolve them. When we repent to the Lord and say we're sorry, and then go back and do the same thing again, we're not really sorry. We set up prayers and fasts and return to the same behavior; we really don't understand the fear of God. To know right and still do wrong is presumptuous sin, and when you keep doing the same thing over and over, you're getting further away from God.

note.label: Pay The Price: Pleasure Now Regret Later

precepts.why:
“Every way of a man is right in his own eyes: but the Lord pondereth the hearts.” A man keeps rehearsing the same sin over and over, and in his own eyes he thinks he is walking right. When you keep doing the same thing over and over, you are getting further away from God. Watch what the same chapter says: “The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.”

You are wandering away from God. You keep doing the same thing over and over and over and wonder why life is not working out for you. This is what spiritual men and women are supposed to examine: things aren't working right right now; could it be that you have a secret life?

They thought sacrifice was going to absolve them, but “To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to the Lord than sacrifice.” We repent to the Lord, Lord, we're sorry, then go back and do the same thing again: we're not really sorry. We set up prayers and fasts and return to the same behavior, because we don't really understand the fear of God. To know right and still do wrong is presumptuous sin, and we've all been guilty of it. But there has to be a day we stop, or we won't receive the kingdom.

So we all want the kingdom? Then we have to change on this end. We can't wait and think we'll become somebody different in the kingdom. Bring forth fruits meet for repentance, or remain with the congregation of the dead.

precepts.text: To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to the Lord than sacrifice.
precepts.point: Whosoever shall keep the whole law and yet offend in one point is guilty of all: the Christian says you cannot keep them, but the context is the royal law, as the next verse shows, he that said do not commit adultery said also do not kill. Speak and do as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty, since Christ redeemed us from the death the moral law carried; he shall have judgment without mercy that hath showed no mercy.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
“To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to the Lord than sacrifice.”

To do justice and judgment, just like the Lord told Saul to do, is more acceptable than sacrifice. He says it over and over and over again: in Samuel, in the Psalms, in Mark, and here in Proverbs.

Justice and judgment is how you treat your neighbour. In James 2 the assembly seated the rich man in a good place and told the poor man to stand there, and James asks, “Are ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?” That is the opposite of doing justice and judgment, and no sacrifice would make up for it. Keeping the royal law is what is acceptable to the Lord.

precepts.text: The most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will.
precepts.point: The Most High ruleth in the kingdom of men and setteth up over it the basest of men.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

precepts.why:
“The king’s heart is in the hand of the Lord, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.” The king in this nation right now, in 2026, is Donald Trump. His heart is in the hand of the Lord, and whatever way the Lord wants him to go, he is going to go, and he is going to fulfill what the Lord has in store.

Daniel shows why: “This matter is by the decree of the watchers, and the demand by the word of the holy ones: to the intent that the living may know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men.” God rules in the kingdoms of men. God is the ultimate ruler.

And what does he do? He “giveth it to whomsoever he will, and setteth up over it the basest of men.” He gives the kingdom over to whomever he chooses, and he sets over it the basest of men: the least of men, the bottom feeders. The bottom feeders are ruling us right now. Biden, Trump, Putin, all of them: they are the bottom.

So the king’s heart turning like rivers of water and the Most High setting up the basest of men are the same truth. Trump is not ruling by his own power. He is set up by the Most High and turned whithersoever he will, a sword in the hand of God to bring judgment on the nations.

precepts.text: The king's heart is in the hand of the Lord.
precepts.point: The Most High ruleth in the kingdom of men and setteth up over it the basest of men. God allows what Trump is doing.

note.label: America Hedgemony & Oppression

precepts.why:
Daniel says “the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will”, and Solomon shows how: “The king’s heart is in the hand of the Lord, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.” God turns the king's heart wherever he will. Whatever the Lord wants the king to do, he is going to do it.

So even in these last days, God gave who is ruling the world today. America is the superpower, and God put Trump in that position. Everything you see Trump doing today, God is allowing it. He is snatching people up off the street and sending them to prisons in other countries, and that is not outside the hand of the Most High.

This answers the question our people ask: why is God allowing Trump to do the things being done on the earth? Because the heart of that king is in the Lord's hand, and the Most High is setting up over the kingdom of men whom he will, even “the basest of men”, to bring his judgment to pass.

precepts.point: You do not regard it, and then you want the wise to carry you.

precepts.point: Each of them made the image of Jesus in his own heart, and that is not the God this vision is about.

note.label: Ezekiel 37:1-11 | Excerpt from “The 4 Temples of Jerusalem”

precepts.text: The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead. There is a reason why, when you look at those old photos, you look run down, tired. You are twenty-one years old looking forty. This is supposed to be the pinnacle of life, of your youth. And we wandered out of the way of understanding, and we were like the walking dead. They make those movies mocking us. We were the congregation of the dead. And it is ironic that zombies walk groping. That is groping at noonday. That is what the Lord said: you break my commandments and you are going to be groping, walking around trying to catch on to something, gravitate to something. All confused in the spirit. Even though the sun is at the apex, you cannot see. We were blinded. We were distracted.
precepts.point: All they that keep it shall come to life. That is just like us. Do you ever look at your old pictures and old videos from when you were in the world? You look dead. You look spiritually dead. That is why the Bible says the law is a spirit. The commandments are spirit.

note.label: Ignite Your Influence

precepts.why:
Baruch says the law “endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” Since the beginning of time this law has been in place. Break it and judgments come upon you; keep it and blessings come upon you. Solomon shows what happens to those who leave it: “The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.”

Look at your old pictures and old videos from when you were in the world. You look dead, spiritually dead. Run down and tired, twenty-one years old looking forty, when that was supposed to be the pinnacle of life, of your youth. We wandered out of the way of understanding, and we were like the walking dead. That is why the law is called a spirit: the commandments are spirit, and without them there is no life in us.

They make those movies mocking us. We were the congregation of the dead. And it is ironic that zombies walk groping. That is groping at noonday, what the Lord said would come on us for breaking his commandments: walking around trying to catch on to something, gravitate to something, all confused in the spirit. Even with the sun at its apex we could not see. We were blinded. We were distracted.

So the law is the difference between the living and the dead. Those who keep it come to life, the way we did when we came into this truth; those who wander from it remain in the congregation of the dead.

precepts.text: There is treasure to be desired in the dwelling of the wise, but a foolish man spendeth it up.
precepts.point: A prudent man foresees the evil coming and makes preparation so he is not consumed in it; the simple pass on and are punished. There is treasure and oil in the dwelling of the wise, but a foolish man spends it up; spending irrationally is a spirit of folly.

note.label: Genesis 41: Pharaoh's Dreams and Joseph's Rise Over Egypt

precepts.why:
“There is treasure to be desired and oil in the dwelling of the wise; but a foolish man spendeth it up.” Joseph’s counsel was the counsel of the wise: gather all the food of the good years, lay up corn under the hand of Pharaoh, and keep it in store against the seven years of famine. The treasure stays in the dwelling of the wise so Egypt could ration food through the famine.

A foolish man spends it up. Spending irrationally is a spirit of folly; had Egypt eaten through the plenty of the seven good years, it would have perished in the seven lean ones.

precepts.text: The king's heart is in the hand of the Lord; he turns rulers whithersoever he will, no matter who is voted in.
precepts.point: The things that were written aforetime were written for our learning, and the thing that hath been is that which shall be. That is why so many similarities appear between the captivities: this captivity carries the marks of Egypt, of Babylon, and of the Greeks, because these things must come to pass.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

precepts.why:
“I have hardened his heart, and the heart of his servants, that I might shew these my signs before him”. The Most High hardened Pharaoh and his servants so that he might show his signs and exemplify his power in the earth, and after he brought down Egypt and delivered the people, every nation feared Israel and the God of Israel.

He could do that because Pharaoh's heart was his to turn. “The king’s heart is in the hand of the Lord, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.” He is in control of the mind of the kings of the world. So there is no need to worry over who becomes president or who gets put in office; either way the Most High is in control.

The same holds in spiritual Egypt today. He will harden the hearts of the rulers of this kingdom so they will not let Israel go and will continue to oppress. It does not matter who is voted into office; whoever sits in the seat, the Most High turns him about like the rivers of water.

precepts.text: There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against the Lord; everything ultimately works within his plan.
precepts.point: The Most High is in control of everything, good and evil alike. Even affliction that comes on his people is his tactic to make them seek him and repent; nothing anybody does can alter the outcome he has already ordained, for he declared the end from the beginning.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

precepts.why: “There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against the Lord.” The Philistines had dominion over Israel and Samson was chasing their daughters, yet none of it stood against the Lord: everything ultimately works within his plan. He sought an occasion against the Philistines through Samson’s own lust, and nothing anybody does, Samson, his parents or the Philistines, can alter the outcome he has already ordained, for he declared the end from the beginning.

precepts.text: The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination: how much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind? It does not merely do nothing; it makes the Most High more angry, and Saul probably would have kept those animals to eat had it never been pointed out.
precepts.point: Samuel makes it plain: Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams. Do you think the Lord prefers a sacrifice to atone for broken commandments over you simply keeping the commandments? That is a heavy verse.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

precepts.why:
“The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination: how much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind?” Such a sacrifice does not merely do nothing; it makes the Most High more angry.

Saul probably would have kept those animals to eat had it never been pointed out.

precepts.text: The king's heart is in the hand of the Lord, and he turneth it whithersoever he will.
precepts.point: Then God changed the spirit of the king into mildness. He leaped from his throne, took her in his arms until she came to herself, and comforted her with loving words. The Most High turned the king's heart.

note.label: Esther 15: Esther Before the King

precepts.why:
The king looked very fiercely upon her and she fainted; then God changed the spirit of the king into mildness. He leaped from his throne, took her in his arms until she came to herself, and comforted her with loving words.

“The king’s heart is in the hand of the Lord, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.” That is what happened between the fierce look and the loving words. The Most High turned the king's heart. The one law was to put her to death, and the king was very dreadful, but his heart was not his own to keep hard; it is in the hand of the Lord, and he turned it for Esther and for his people.

precepts.text: When the scorner is punished the simple is made wise; that is making wise the simple.
precepts.point: Making wise the simple: pay attention to who the simple is, the scorner, the foolish, the youth void of understanding. A lot of times we go out and think the scorner is somebody who does not want to hear, but it also goes into a youth who thinks he knows something but really does not.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“When the scorner is punished, the simple is made wise: and when the wise is instructed, he receiveth knowledge.” When the scorner is punished, the simple is made wise. That is “making wise the simple” in Psalm 19:7.

Again the scorner and the simple are the same one. The testimony of the Lord is sure, and it makes the simple wise.

precepts.text: The king's heart is in the hand of the Most High, as the rivers of water he turneth it whithersoever he will.
precepts.point: Sisters forced to wear pants at work should keep a skirt or dress in the car or book bag, change in the bathroom on the way out if they can, and ask the Most High for mercy; these are things done in captivity.

note.label: Psalm 47: God the Great King Over All the Earth

precepts.why:
“God reigneth over the heathen: God sitteth upon the throne of his holiness.” How does he reign over them? “The king’s heart is in the hand of the Lord, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.”

The Most High rules in the realm of men and turns the king's heart wherever he wills. He put it on the spirit of the nations to release the slaves, to institute laws, to bring judgment, and also to give Israel favor. So Israel should fear him and not the nations; whatever the nations do to Israel is of the Most High, whose hand holds the king's heart.

precepts.text: A man's way is not in himself; his steps are directed by the Most High.
precepts.point: Man's goings are of the Most High. A lot of us were guided into the truth and do not understand it. You did not come in just because a friend shared a flyer or you found a random YouTube video. It was not random.

note.label: Proverbs 21: The Most High Rules the Heart of the King

precepts.why:
“The king’s heart is in the hand of the Lord, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.” The mind of the king is controlled by the Most High. Just as Pharaoh's heart was hardened against Moses and Israel, the Most High can harden the hearts of kings and soften them, and he used heathen kings to deal in our favor, like Cyrus in the time of Ezra, who did things in favor of our people.

Jeremiah says it is not only kings: “O Lord, I know that the way of man is not in himself: it is not in man that walketh to direct his steps.” A man's way is not in himself; his steps are directed by the Most High. Man's goings are of the Most High.

A lot of us were guided into the truth and do not understand it. You did not come in just because a friend shared a flyer or you found a random YouTube video. It was not random. The same hand that turns the king's heart directed your steps here.

Every way of a man is right in his own eyes, but the Most High weighs the heart, and he is the one directing the steps.

precepts.text: A fool's lips enter into contention and his mouth calls for strokes because he says disrespectful things.
precepts.point: A proud and haughty scorner is his name, who deals in proud wrath.

note.label: Proverbs 21: The Most High Rules the Heart of the King

precepts.why:
“Whoso keepeth his mouth and his tongue keepeth his soul from troubles.” Often it is your mouth that gets you into trouble.

Solomon already said how: “A fool’s lips enter into contention, and his mouth calleth for strokes.” The fool's mouth calls for strokes because he says disrespectful things. People get knocked out on World Star because they did not know how to shut up; they disrespected the wrong one and ran their mouth. All they had to do was say it was not worth fighting over.

When we get annoyed we want to slap somebody, and it is biblical, the mouth calls for strokes. But we control our spirit and do not put hands on anybody. Keep your mouth and your tongue and you keep your soul from that trouble; that is the difference between the man who keeps his mouth and the proud and haughty scorner who deals in proud wrath.

precepts.text: The diligent tend to plenteousness while the lazy come to want.
precepts.point: See a man diligent in business; he will stand before kings, not before mean men. To deal among the upper echelon you have to be diligent.

note.label: Proverbs 22: A Good Name and Training Up a Child

precepts.why:
“Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.” To deal among the upper echelon you have to be diligent.

Solomon shows where diligence and laziness each lead: “The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; but of every one that is hasty only to want.” The diligent tend to plenteousness while the lazy come to want. Even the thoughts of the diligent man are headed toward plenty.

That plenty is what carries a man before kings instead of mean men. Diligence in business is the way up, and want is where hastiness ends.

“The king’s heart is in the hand of the Lord, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.” He turns Netanyahu, Kim Jong-un, and every ruler wherever he wills, and one day he will activate them to self-destruct.

That is how a snare is laid for Babylon and “thou art also taken, O Babylon, and thou wast not aware: thou art found, and also caught, because thou hast striven against the Lord.” “The Lord hath opened his armoury, and hath brought forth the weapons of his indignation”. Every missile, nuke, and bomb these nations think they own, the Most High calls his armory. A black man, the Most High God, and his son Christ are the most powerful beings, and all that the nations possess belongs to him.

So “the hammer of the whole earth” is cut asunder and broken, and Babylon becomes a desolation among the nations, because the kings' hearts that hold the weapons are in his hand.
